# Security policy

Affirmers ties social activity to coins built for Solana. Because value will eventually move through its programs, security reports are taken seriously and handled privately.

## Reporting a vulnerability

Do not open a public issue for a security problem. Contact the maintainers through the security contact once the team publishes it on the site. Until a contact is stated, hold the report and do not disclose it publicly.

Please include:

- what you found and where
- steps to reproduce, or a proof of concept
- the impact you expect
- whether you have shared it with anyone else

You can expect an acknowledgement, an assessment, and a fix timeline proportional to severity. Please allow a reasonable period for a fix before any public discussion.

## Scope

In scope:

- the site source and build output in this repository
- the content security policy and headers it ships with
- the on-chain programs, once their addresses are published

Out of scope:

- third-party services the site reads from (the Solana RPC provider, DefiLlama, DexScreener)
- social engineering of maintainers
- reports that only say a header or setting differs from a personal preference

## Verifying the right address

Impersonation is the most common attack in this space. The contract address appears only at the top of the official site, and only after the team states it. Treat any other source of an address with suspicion, and compare it against the site before interacting.

## What we never ask for

Seed phrases, private keys, or wallet files. Nobody on the team will request them.

## Safe harbour

Good-faith research that avoids privacy violations, data destruction and service disruption, and that stops at proof of concept, will not be pursued.
